overview: Bind a proven CRDT model to a rich-text editor; persist local updates before showing saved locally, then exchange missing operations using state vectors. Presence is ephemeral and throttled. Undo tracks local user operations rather than reverting the whole shared snapshot. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.result: Throttle/coalesce remote cursor presentation; durable document operations require a separate reliable path
estimation.implication: Profile long-document typing and IME; presence rate is an assumption, not an algorithm correctness proof.

components.purpose: Bind a proven CRDT model to a rich-text editor; persist local updates before showing saved locally, then exchange missing operations using state vectors. Presence is ephemeral and throttled. Undo tracks local user operations rather than reverting the whole shared snapshot. Performance plan: Document with 50 concurrent editors and 100,000 characters; incremental operations and bounded presence rendering. Accessibility: Use an editor with documented keyboard/screen-reader and IME support; toolbar buttons expose pressed state, shortcuts and focus return. Announce connection status without rereading every remote edit. Failure recovery: Revalidate permissions before sync; preserve a recoverable local copy and explain rejected writes. CRDT convergence does not solve authorization or semantic conflicts. Trade-off: Server-ordered OT is a valid alternative with transform/version machinery. Last-write-wins whole-document replacement loses concurrent edits and is unsuitable here.

failureCases.scenario: Offline edits meet remote edits after permissions were revoked

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
